summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2E.1 -- HHCE-001 + Trust-Enrollment Implementation Plan Independent Verification. FINAL DISPOSITION: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- IMPLEMENTATION-READY. Verification-only phase; zero Dell mutation, zero production .py bytes modified, zero contract-text bytes modified. Entering state re-confirmed by direct read, not assumed: HPSE-001 v1.1 (74 requirements, mechanically re-extracted, sequential, no gaps, no duplicates), HBDC-001 v1.2, HHCE-001 v1.0 (52 requirements, mechanically re-extracted, sequential, no gaps, no duplicates), RepositoryIdentity 0107866f-af7c-40b4-8317-74e71acb05ca independently verified, DeploymentBinding absent, Protected Root empty. Housekeeping performed as ordinary governed lifecycle before phase-substantive work: closed the stale idle-placeholder active task, then discovered and closed 31 additional stale, never-closed idle-placeholder task files in tasks/active/ (a known repo bug spanning the 149O.19-149O.20L range), reducing active_task_count from 32 to 1. Read directly this phase, not merely re-narrated from the prior phase's own report: hatp_hardware_credentials.py (HardwareCredentialRecord's exact 5-field schema re-confirmed, no revoked_at field exists today), hatp_fido2_provider.py (credential_identity() re-confirmed a single unconditional raise at the exact cited line range; request_signature()/verify() re-confirmed NOT placeholders -- real CTAP2 device-enumeration, assertion, and COSE-key signature-verification logic already exists), hatp_piv_provider.py (every method, not just credential_identity(), re-confirmed unconditionally fails), hatp_providers.py, hatp_bootstrap.py (PrincipalRecord's exact 2-field schema and _require_revoked_at_consistency's exact reused logic re-confirmed), hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py (the atomic-write/read-back/lock/preview/audit idioms HHCE-001 commits to reusing re-confirmed real and already exercised by passing tests), human_approval_trusted_provenance.py (re-confirmed zero references to HATPHardwareCredentialStore -- the hardware-credential registry is consumed exclusively inside a provider's own verify(), never by verify_hatp_proof directly), hatp_signing_ceremony.py (the credential_identity() reuse-for-enrollment claim re-confirmed at its exact cited line), and HPSE-001 v1.1's full 52-section text plus HBDC-001 v1.2's Protected Root/timestamp-grammar sections. Independently re-verified NBF-2 (revoked_at semantics) structurally closed: HHCE-REQ-008..011 reuse hatp_bootstrap.py's already-implemented _require_revoked_at_consistency function and the identical HBDC-REQ-067 timestamp grammar, both re-confirmed present verbatim; monotonicity re-confirmed against revoke_deployment_binding's real, already-implemented behavior. Independently re-verified NBF-1 (continuous two-lock hold) is closed by explicit contract text (HHCE-REQ-037) -- correctly identified that full structural re-verification against running code cannot occur this phase because no writer implementing it exists yet, and is correctly deferred to the next implementation-IV phase (149O.20L.7O.2F.1), which this phase confirms is the right place for it, not a gap in this phase's own scope. Independently re-derived, not accepted from the plan's table, that FIDO2 remains the correct first-provider selection: Fido2HardwareProvider's request_signature/verify are real, only credential_identity() is a placeholder, while PivHardwareProvider's every method unconditionally fails; the fido2 package is declared as an installed extra and directly imported, while no PKCS#11/smart-card dependency exists anywhere in this codebase, confirmed by direct import attempts and grep. Independently re-derived the Surface A-E bundling verdict from the governing prompt's own criteria (shared trust boundary, shared cross-registry invariant, one coherent functional capability, testable together, no independent authority-transition boundary) rather than accepting the plan's own conclusion -- confirmed all five surfaces share HPSE-REQ-056's single cross-registry precondition as their coupling mechanism and none exposes an independent authority-transition boundary; no fragmentation required. Attacked the six-case HPSE-REQ-058 partial-failure matrix, the cross-registry invariant (HPSE-REQ-056/HHCE-REQ-039..041), the writer API's idempotency/conflict disposition (compared directly against create_deployment_binding's real implementation), atomic persistence, lock path/order/deadlock-freedom (traced every Surface A-E operation for acquisition direction; confirmed no reverse-order path exists), revocation semantics, the error vocabulary's non-overlap across HHCE-001/HPSE-001, runtime neutrality (grep-reconfirmed zero claude/codex/deepseek references in src/pcae/core/hatp_*.py), and public-first compliance (grep-reconfirmed zero private-key/secret markers in the contract or plan text). Found zero Blocking findings. Recorded one new Non-Blocking finding (NBF-149O.20L.7O.2E.1-1): HHCE-REQ-002 describes HardwareCredentialRecord.public_key as 'DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo', but Fido2HardwareProvider.verify() (hatp_fido2_provider.py:389) actually parses it as CBOR-encoded COSE_Key bytes (CoseKey.parse(cbor.decode(record.public_key))), independently confirmed against the existing, already-passing test harness's own fixture construction (fido2_cbor.encode(dict(cose_key))). Classified Non-Blocking because the mismatch fails closed (a DER-encoded value would raise inside verify()'s broad except, yielding signature_valid=False, never a security hole) and because the companion implementation plan's own Surface A text already independently describes the correct COSE format, so an implementer following the full contract-plus-plan bundle is not misled in practice. Recommended a fix-in-passing correction to HHCE-001 Section 5 during 149O.20L.7O.2F, not a dedicated repair phase, per the instruction to avoid creating repair phases for editorial issues. Recorded two Observations: fast_green suite run-to-run variance across three consecutive runs against an unmodified tree (284/285/294 failed), consistent with this repository's already-documented task-lifecycle-concurrent-run flakiness, resolved via a full node-ID deselect confirmation run; and the fido2 package's absence from this development environment, already disclosed by prior phases, re-confirmed not new. Final verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- IMPLEMENTATION-READY. Real registration, real enrollment, real provisioning, real DeploymentBinding creation, real certification, and real HATP activation all remain not authorized. Recommended next: 149O.20L.7O.2F -- HATP Trust-Enrollment Implementation Capability, then 149O.20L.7O.2F.1 -- its own Independent Verification. See docs/PHASE_149O_20L_7O_2E_1_HHCE_TRUST_ENROLLMENT_PLAN_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md for full detail.
